slides.headline: At 11 years old, she just broke a chess record that stood for over two decades.
Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest Woman Grandmaster in chess history, at age 11
slides.body: Playing top board for England at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, she secured her third and final WGM norm - breaking a record held jointly by Kateryna Lagno and future Women's World Champion Hou Yifan, both of whom earned the title at age 12.

slides.headline: She played all 11 rounds on England's top board - and scored 8 points doing it.
slides.body: Born in India, based in Harrow, UK, she took up chess as a hobby during the COVID-19 pandemic. In July 2025, at age 10, she had already become the youngest player ever to earn a WGM norm - breaking a record previously held by Hou Yifan.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A record that stood for two decades just fell to an 11-year-old who started during a pandemic.
slides.body: A Viksit Bharat by 2047 is built partly on stories like this - proof that talent with Indian roots keeps setting the pace globally, in fields nobody would have predicted a generation ago.
